title: Type Conversion and Coercion knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best demonstrates understanding of “Type Conversion and Coercion”?
options: Use Type Conversion and Coercion deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
Assume Ruby automatically guarantees every business rule and external system behavior.
Replace all built-in features with a third-party framework regardless of the task.
Skip tests because a short example ran once.
questions.answer_key: Use Type Conversion and Coercion deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
questions.explanation: Use Type Conversion and Coercion deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: When applying “Type Conversion and Coercion”, which practice is the most reliable?
options: Silence all errors and trust the result without inspecting inputs.
Use unrelated global state so every part of the program can modify the same value.
Treat all Ruby versions and third-party dependencies as identical.
Keep the type conversion and coercion rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Keep the type conversion and coercion rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Keep the type conversion and coercion rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: If a result involving “Type Conversion and Coercion” differs from your prediction, what should you do first?
options: Disable validation or security checks to make the example pass faster.
Change several unrelated lines at once and avoid reproducing the problem.
When behavior differs from your prediction, reproduce the smallest case, inspect the diagnostic, and check the supported documentation before changing code.
Catch every exception and continue even if the program state is unknown.
questions.answer_key: When behavior differs from your prediction, reproduce the smallest case, inspect the diagnostic, and check the supported documentation before changing code.
questions.explanation: When behavior differs from your prediction, reproduce the smallest case, inspect the diagnostic, and check the supported documentation before changing code. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.
